identity.real_world_identity_notes: McLaren MP4/6, the Honda RA121/E V12 car in which Ayrton Senna took the 1991 title. Wikipedia records it as the last Formula One car to win a World Championship using a manual transmission, on a Weismann/McLaren transverse six-speed manual gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The cockpit disagrees with itself. The visible lever and its animation are those of a sequential stick, while the gearbox accepts direct gear selection, which a sequential cannot do, and needs the driver to match revs. The mechanism is recorded as an H-pattern because that is what the gearbox does and what the real car had; the sequential-looking lever is treated as a modelling detail rather than evidence about the transmission.

The gate is recorded unknown for the same reason. A lever animated as a sequential cannot be read for a gate, and no reviewed source describes the MP4/6's shift pattern, so neither the cockpit nor the sources establish it.
Gearbox construction is not established either. The source names Weismann/McLaren but not its engagement, so the downshift blip stays unknown.

Clutch telemetry was present while the running shifts were accepted as clutchless. The channel cannot separate the pedal from the clutch the car works itself, so the accepted results stand; the driver confirmed no pedal was used.

This class mixes technologies, which is period-correct. Teams adopted semi-automatic gearboxes at different times around 1990, so a manual car and a paddle car raced in the same field. Nothing is inherited between models on the strength of a shared class.

Only the high-downforce identity was observed. AMS2 selects the aero configuration from the circuit, so this car reports a different identity at a low-downforce track; that identity is not recorded here because it has not been observed and an exact match cannot be guessed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mclaren-honda-mp4-6-high-downforce.20260815t040832936z-f73b08c6 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the MP4/6 and its manual gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

Wikipedia gives a Weismann/McLaren transverse 6-speed manual and records the car as the last champion with a manual transmission. The live drive selected six gears with no automatic cut or blip and accepted direct gear selection, both of which agree with a manual gearbox.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Weismann/McLaren transverse six-speed - the last gearbox to win a Formula One title without paddles. Neither how it engages nor the gate layout is recorded, so blip on downshifts to be safe.

deviations.basis: Whether the driver must blip on downshifts is not established. A guided drive settles what the simulator requires; where the real car differs, that difference is recorded as an override rather than changing this value.

The gearbox type is not established. A guided drive cannot separate a synchromesh from a dog box, so unlike the other open fields this one is closed by a reviewed source rather than by driving the car.

The gate is not established. It is read from the cockpit by watching the lever and the driver's hand through a shift, the method that read three dogleg gates in dataset 0.3.28 and that registered sources then corroborated.
